entries.test: Published evaluations and research available by October 2023 would show whether hallucinations were a widely recognized, characteristic failure of systems that generalize based on word distributions.
entries.note: “Hallmark” has a plain reading as a characteristic failure, without requiring every output to hallucinate.
The compound claim combines an undefined standard of understanding with a judgment about trustworthiness. The authors’ public reaffirmation does not make those judgments objectively settleable.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and technical descriptions of 1970s AI and contemporary LLMs would establish their comparative task breadth and reliance on manual customization, including human feedback.
entries.note: Despite the evaluative phrase “incredible advance,” the passage supplies concrete comparisons and preserves the qualification “generally.”

entries.test: The public post and its quoted Hoffman statement establish whether Marcus offered $100,000 to take the opposing side of that bet.
entries.note: The normalized proposition faithfully records a public wager offer. Offering the bet is not itself a firm forecast that Hoffman's outcome will fail.
